focus.signature: def capture(source, max_events=2000, progress=False, compile_only=False, live=False, validate_only=False):

context.paragraph: runtime/capture.py#capture accepts a small syntax/builtin surface and checks a 16 KiB source cap and 256 Python lexical tokens before execution. The token cap excludes whitespace, comments, and indentation. Sharing uses the same tokenizer in validation-only mode without parsing or executing the program. The native capture utility enforces event, object-identity, activation, and output limits. Browser live mode has no total event limit: completed frames are released, object identities use a bounded registry with monotonic IDs, and output retains its latest 4,096 characters. Evicted objects may receive new IDs if observed again; IDs are never reassigned to unrelated objects. Active/suspended activations remain capped at 256. Async functions, await, public attributes, and public standard-library imports are accepted. Third-party imports, relative imports, private attributes, classes, generators, and exception-handling syntax remain rejected. Module availability depends on the bundled WASM build; unsupported OS facilities can still fail at runtime. The source-size cap is independent of runtime cost.

otherReferences.paragraph: runtime/capture.py#capture includes an additive parsing artifact in capture schema 2. Records distinguish rule checkpoints, cursor rewinds, and tokens with kind, text, and source start coordinates. These are actual parser token requests, not a second Python tokenize pass presented as internal activity. Tokenization errors during the size precheck are deferred to the real parser, preserving syntax-failure traces.
